text.p: Matches scheduled in the Italian Serie A on Sunday (league standings in brackets, kick-offs GMT):

Milan, boosted by a 2-0 win against Fiorentina last week and without suspended Yugoslav midfielder Dejan Savicevic, again drop Roberto Baggio, relying on Liberian George Weah and Marco Simone in attack. Atalanta look to Domenico Morfeo, Gigi Lentini and leading goalscorer Filippo Inzaghi to compensate for the disappointment of a 3-2 loss to Lazio last week.

Cup Winners' Cup semifinalists Fiorentina were most unimpressive in their 1-0 quarter-final second leg defeat by Portugal's Benfica on Thursday. If they continue in that vein it will be a walk-over for Parma. Cup-tied Russian winger Andrei Kanchelskis and midfielder Sandro Cois return for Fiorentina while in-form Parma welcome back Croatian midfielder Mario Stanic but will be without Massimo Crippa and Dino Baggio, both suspended.

Statistics reveal that over the last 40 years, Verona have scored one goal every 7-1/2 hours at the San Siro. They look sure to continue that negative trend on Sunday against a full-strength Inter boosted by Tuesday's UEFA Cup semifinal qualification at the expense of Belgium's Anderlecht.

More than 75,000 fans will be at the San Paolo for one of the occasions of the season. In a week in which coach Luigi Simoni announced his end-of-season resignation, Napoli have a lot to prove. Brazilian Andre Cruz and Frenchman Alain Boghossian are doubtful starters for Napoli, while Juventus will be without suspended Yugoslav midfielder Vladimir Jugovic and injured striker Alessandro Del Piero. In their absence, Brazilian Beto and Fabio Pecchia orchestrate the Napoli midfield while Michele Padovano and Nicola Amoruso lead the Juventus attack.

A desperate relegation battle between two teams with the same number of points. Perugia's Brazilian Muller is out through injury leaving Croat Milan Rapajic and Marco Negri to lead the attack, while defenders Alberto Di Chiara and Marco Materazzi are both suspended. Cagliari will be without injured Uruguayan midfielder Fabian O'Neill, leaving compatriot Dario Silva to lead the attack along with Sandro Tovalieri.

Sampdoria could do Piacenza's relegation rivals, Perugia and Cagliari, a big favour if they win here. Although Yugoslav Sinisa Mihajlovic is suspended, Sampdoria look strong with Frenchman Christian Karembeu and Argentine Juan Veron in midfield and captain Roberto Mancini in attack. Piacenza rely on their regular attack of Pasquale Luiso and Gian Pietro Piovani.

With 10 games left, time is running out for bottom club Reggiana. Visitors Udinese are unlikely to be charitable, while their strike force of Brazilian Amoroso and German Oliver Bierhoff is potentially lethal. Reggiana look to Colombian Adolfo Valencia and Russian Igor Simutenkov in attack.

A game with implications for UEFA Cup places next season. Buoyant Bologna may be encouraged by Roma's comprehensive 3-0 loss to Juventus last week. Argentine Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti lead the Roma attack while Bologna field their regular forward trio of Carlo Nervo, Swede Kennet Andersson and Russian Igor Kolyvanov.

Another game with UEFA Cup implications. With Pierluigi Casiraghi and Giuseppe Signori out through injury and Igor Protti suspended, Lazio field an unusual attack of Roberto Rambaudi and Renato Buso. Vicenza, without suspended Uruguayan Gustavo Mendez, rely on his compatriot Marcelo Otero and Roberto Murgita in attack.
